meta_description: Streaming platforms live on two curves: engagement (personalization, discovery, retention) and unit economics (encoding, delivery, churn).

blocks.x: Streaming platforms live on two curves: engagement (personalization, discovery, retention) and unit economics (encoding, delivery, churn). Both are decision engines — and both run better on governed telemetry, evaluation-driven ML and cost telemetry.

The workflows we industrialize here: Personalization/discovery, Subscriber lifecycle, Delivery cost management, Experimentation, Anti-piracy. Each arrives with its current cycle times measured in the Diagnose phase, and each leaves the program governed by outcome SLOs rather than anecdotes.

items: Recommendations plateau without governance over objectives (engagement vs. satisfaction).
View definitions, session metrics and retention measures inconsistent; product decisions wobble.
Cost per stream/hour by CDN/region/codec unknown; margin leaks.
Password sharing and stream-ripping drain ARPU; enforcement blunt.
Cancellation intents handled at save-desk; churn prediction un-wired to actions.
Experiment platform bottlenecks; product teams queue.
